pr.title: Keep Codex delivery through idle unloads and repair lost acknowledgments
pr.head: e8851ec6f46428968a3ffb7c3eb4846d25e0bad3

summary: Projector's watch daemon delivers pull request events to a Codex session. It sends each batch, a group of event lines with a unique ID, with codex queue --thread <id> --message <text> --resume. That command loads the conversation again if Codex has unloaded it. Codex's hooks call project watch codex-hook at each step of the session. The UserPromptSubmit hook acknowledges a batch when its turn starts, and the daemon sends the next batch only after that acknowledgment.

Two faults stopped delivery. First, Codex sends SessionEnd when it unloads a conversation that has been idle for 30 minutes, and also when you archive, delete, or exit one. Its reason field cannot tell these apart. Projector switched delivery off on every SessionEnd, so an idle unload turned off the very wake-up that --resume exists for. Second, one batch reached Codex and ran, but its acknowledgment never arrived. The daemon never resends a batch Codex accepted, so every later batch for that session waited behind it.

1. SessionEnd only records the unload. Delivery stays on, and watch status shows unloaded_at. Every hook from the session's own conversation records the transcript_path Codex gives it. Codex moves or removes that file when you archive or delete the conversation, so a missing transcript makes the session lapse everywhere.
  2. The transcript confirms a lost acknowledgment. Every 30 seconds the daemon reads what the transcript gained since a queued or uncertain batch was submitted. It marks the batch consumed once the batch's marker appears there.
The plugin's hooks.json stays unchanged, so users do not have to trust Projector's hooks again.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Batch: one message the daemon sends to Codex, opened by PROJECTOR WATCH <batch id> and a session= line.
  • Acknowledgment: the UserPromptSubmit hook matching a batch's prompt, which writes a receipt and deletes the pending batch.
  • Unload: Codex freeing an idle conversation from memory. queue --resume loads it again.
  • Transcript: Codex's JSONL record of a conversation, the rollout-…-<thread id>.jsonl file.
  • Lapsed: no longer counted as live, so the daemon sends nothing and a registered agent stops showing in agent list.

groups.title: Delivery survives an unload, and the transcript confirms lost acknowledgments
groups.kicker: How hooks, the lease, and the dispatcher treat an ended or archived conversation
intro: codex_watch.py holds Codex delivery: the registration in codex.json, the hook handler, and the Dispatcher that the daemon ticks about once a second. A registration is active while it is enabled, its 24-hour lease has not expired, and, from this change on, its recorded transcript still exists.

The hook handler now routes every hook except SessionStart through note. note renews the lease, except on SessionEnd, and records the transcript. It sets unloaded_at on SessionEnd and clears it on any other hook. own_transcript keeps a subagent's transcript out, because a subagent's hooks carry the parent's session ID.

For a batch whose acknowledgment is lost, Dispatcher.confirm runs at most every 30 seconds per session. It calls delivered, which reads the transcript from the byte offset recorded when the batch was submitted. The search string is the batch marker and session line, written as JSON-escaped text.

checks.text: The transcript cannot confirm a batch before its hook runs. Real Codex transcripts on the reviewing machine show the batch's user message written right after the UserPromptSubmit hook's output, so the hook acknowledges first. Every record that carries a batch marker lies inside that batch's own queue-triggered turn.
An archived session's registration stays enabled. append_events keeps queuing its events into codex-events.json, and they go out once the conversation is resumed. Nothing is dropped.

files.note: Adds own_transcript, gone, note, consume, delivered, and Dispatcher.confirm. It records transcript_offset at each submission and makes active treat a missing transcript as lapsed.

checks.text: transcript_offset is taken under the folder lock before codex queue runs, so text written before the submission cannot confirm the batch.
A batch with no offset, from before this change, scans the whole transcript once. After that, the offset moves to the end, leaving room for a marker that is only partly written.

intro: The completed codex-delivery plan still records that SessionEnd disconnects. A completed plan is a record, so docs/cli.md carries the new behavior instead.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Five new unit tests and a rewritten live smoke test
intro: The unit tests use a fake codex executable that logs its calls, and transcript files in a temporary directory. The live smoke test runs an isolated Codex app server with thread_unload_delay_secs, so Codex sends its own SessionEnd. It then wakes the thread twice and checks that an archived thread gets no batch.

files.note: New tests cover the idle unload, archive and resume, the daemon start on SessionEnd, a lost acknowledgment, and text from before submission.
